criteria.name: brief_fidelity
criteria.description: The premise is recognizably the story the brief asked for — same subject matter, same kind of cast, same spirit. Test: if the brief asked for a family trip and the premise is a corporate conspiracy with a deadline, score 0–25. If someone reading only the premise could guess what the user asked for, score 70+.

criteria.name: central_question
criteria.description: The central_question is a values tension with at least two defensible answers — not a logistics problem. Test: 'can she finish in time?' has one good answer, score 0–35. 'Is holding the family together worth pretending nothing is changing?' can be honestly answered both ways — score 70+. The question must also be one this premise's situation actually argues, not a bolted-on abstraction.

criteria.name: grimgong_test
criteria.description: Each character's situation reads as one particular person, not an archetype with adjectives. 'A gruff warrior haunted by war' fails (0–35); 'a purpose-bred imperial crusher; the war is over and the thing he was built for no longer exists' passes (70+). Specificity must come from the situation, not stacked adjectives. The charge field names something genuinely unresolved or magnetic, and no character exists merely to fill a plot function (no love-interest-by-quota, no designated villain without their own situation).

criteria.name: voice_specificity
criteria.description: Voice descriptions are concrete enough that a writer could imitate the character cold. They must include vocabulary level, sentence length or rhythm, and what breaks under pressure. Test: if voice is only 'speaks softly' or 'uses technical jargon,' score 0–40. If a writer could generate three plausible lines in that character's voice from the description alone, score 70+. Voices must differ from each other.

criteria.name: downstream_utility
criteria.description: All fields populated with specific, usable content. protagonist_id matches a character. appearance_tags have concrete values (not 'unknown'). tone_directives each tie to a specific dialogue behavior. The setting's physical description is specific enough to generate consistent images. No vague placeholder content anywhere.
